results.content: With three months to go until the U.S. midterm elections in November, voters increasingly seem to prefer Democrats over the Republican Party that has had control of Congress for the last two years. Results of a Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday showed that 42% of registered voters would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate at present, compared to 37% for a Republican. The same survey also found that, for the first time in nearly a decade of its polling series, voters perceive the Democratic Party as having a better plan for the economy than the Republican Party. results.content: With less than three months until Election Day, the general election fight for control of the US Senate is in full swing after a summer of upheaval and decisions in Democratic contests. Democrats are leading Republicans on the generic ballot by 8 points, among registered voters, a CNN poll conducted by SSRS showed, and by a 10-point margin, Americans call Democrats more than Republicans “the party of change” – though it is worth noting nearly half say that label does not describe either party. North Carolina remains the state most likely to flip in November with Democratic nominee Roy Cooper in a strong position in the polls and money race against Republican Michael Whatley.
